summary: Fire finder 1929, L-4 house 1933, windstorm 1976, R-6 cab moved in that year, torn down 2007. The summit is a hiking spot with no lookout left.

facts.design: R-6 flat-top cab moved in 1976; earlier L-4 ground house (1933)
facts.status_note: Torn down in 2007. Sources differ on whether the cab was burned in place or salvaged first.

staffing.status: not staffed; lookout removed in 2007; last confirmed staffing August 1990

access.note: NHLR calls the summit a popular hiking and wildflower destination. No current source confirms access.

visit.trail_note: No lookout remains to climb. A 1976 newspaper described the summit as easily accessible by trail.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Willamette National Forest, Sweet Home Ranger District)

events.note: Fire finder placed on the summit (not a cabin).
L-4 ground house built on the summit.
A lookout fireman was named for the season.
Lookout on duty, per a 1940 newspaper item.
House destroyed by a windstorm in February 1976.
R-6 cab moved to the summit from Herman Peak (named Herman Lookout by FFLOS).
A Forest Service fire lookout died after an apparent fall near the cabin in August 1990, so the post was still staffed.
Torn down. NHLR says knocked down and burned in place after vandalism; the 2007 chapter report says members salvaged items first.

corrections.why: The first lookout house was built in 1933 and was destroyed by a windstorm in February 1976. The 1976 date is when the R-6 cab was moved to the summit.
No source read gives a height for the structure, so the value is unsupported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the cab was knocked down and burned in place after vandalism. The 2007 chapter report says members salvaged items before it was brought down. The Oregon lookouts page says it was torn down as a health hazard. All the sources agree on 2007.
The 1976 newspaper and the Oregon lookouts page name Herman Peak; the FFLOS page names Herman Lookout. Both describe the same R-6 cab moved in 1976.
NHLR gives 5,337 ft (1,627 m); FFLOS gives 5,455 ft (1,663 m). The record's 1626.7 m matches NHLR.

notes_for_editor: Core timeline (1929 fire finder, 1933 L-4 house, February 1976 windstorm, 1976 R-6 cab move, 2007 removal) is supported by several sources. Fate is disputed in method, not date. Current status is unverified: no source from after 2007 describes the site, and the planned hiker platform is not confirmed. Height_m 152.4 in the record has no source; remove it. Elevation differs between NHLR and FFLOS. The 1990 death is reported in a historic newspaper item quoted on the Oregon lookouts page; the story names no one. Access is listed as public only on the basis of the 2003 NHLR description.
